{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Interface Licence and Support Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Mortgage Logic.com / "Client") 
**Re:** Contract review findings and recommended redline positions 
**Prepared:** Issues memo based on verified review findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed EXHIBIT 10.4 against our contracting playbook. The agreement is materially vendor-favourable in the two areas that matter most for risk allocation: **indemnity** and **limitation of liability**. TrueLink's indemnity is confined to its own breach or failure to perform, with no duty to defend and no IP infringement, breach of law, data breach or wilful misconduct limbs, while our indemnity in § 12(a) is very broad. The single liability cap is one-sided — it caps TrueLink at 12 months' compensation paid while leaving our liability (including our broad indemnity) entirely uncapped. That combination sits in our walk-away zone and must be corrected.

Several high-severity structural gaps follow: the licence runs to Client alone (excluding affiliates and contractors) and can be terminated for *any* breach of §§ 8(a)–(c) with no materiality or cure right; there is no confirmation that we own our own content, IP or data, or the results of the Support Services; the assignment clause has no M&A successor carve-out, no reasonableness standard on consent and no bar on assignment to our competitors; and our termination right is drafted as a service-continuation mechanic rather than an express convenience right, with a broken cross-reference and no refund of prepaid fees.

At the medium level, § 3(i) imposes a **mandatory sole-source obligation** to order a TrueLink credit report on every borrower underwritten through the Interface — a requirements tie with no cap and no exit for TrueLink performance failure. § 5(a) imposes take-or-pay monthly minimums that § 6 then makes undocumentable and uncontestable. Renewal pricing is uncapped beyond the first-year hosting freeze, there is no post-termination transition assistance or data return/deletion obligation, TrueLink gives no performance warranty (only Y2K) against a full implied-warranty disclaimer, and there is no insurance provision at all.

The agreement is favourable to us in several respects that we should preserve: no liquidated damages or exit fees payable by us; no non-compete or field-of-use restraint (§ 2(a) expressly preserves our freedom to develop or licence competing systems); no vendor-side audit right; no customer-side MFN (the only MFN runs in our favour in § 6); no non-solicit binding us; and California law with San Luis Obispo venue, which is within our accepted list given both parties are California-based.

Two findings carry a failed verification flag (Audit, Non-solicitation). In both cases the underlying analysis concludes the agreement is silent and therefore more favourable than our preferred position; the failed deterministic checks are structurally inapplicable because there is no clause to test. These are watch items, not defects.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue in brief |
|---|----------|------|--------|---------|----------------|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | TrueLink indemnity limited to its breach/failure to perform; no duty to defend, no IP infringement, breach of law, data disclosure or gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs; our § 12(a) indemnity is very broad. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Cap is one-sided (TrueLink capped at 12 months' compensation paid; Client uncapped — walk-away). No mutual indirect-damages exclusion; carve-outs limited to gross negligence/wilful misconduct. |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 15 has only a "financially responsible affiliate" carve-out; no M&A successor carve-out, unqualified consent standard, no bar on assignment to a Client competitor. |
| 4 | High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | § 2(d) protects TrueLink's Interface only; no confirmation we retain Client Content, IP or routed data, and no ownership of Support Services work product (TrueLink's IP definition sweeps in "improvements"). |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No LDs, exit fee or remaining-contract-value payment on termination (§ 14) or non-renewal (§ 13). No redline required. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant runs to Client alone; § 8(c) limits access to Client's own officers/employees/agents; § 13(b) terminates the licence for "any violations or breach" of §§ 8(a)–(c) with no materiality or cure. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint on us; § 2(a) preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or licence competing systems. No redline required. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 14 is a service-continuation mechanic, not an express convenience right; indeterminate notice (30–60 days), subject to a non-existent "Section 4", no refund of prepaid fees; § 13 mis-cross-references § 12. |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review *(verification: fail)* | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No vendor audit/inspection/records right exists; silence is better than our preferred position. Failed frequency-cap check is a false signal — no clause to test. Watch item only. |
| 10 | Medium | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | § 3(i) requires Client to order a TrueLink credit report for every borrower underwritten via the Interface — an uncapped sole-source tie for the full term with no exit for TrueLink performance failure. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Cl. 26 California law; cl. 27 exclusive venue San Luis Obispo County; no arbitration. Within accepted parameters. No redline required. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | Only MFN runs in our favour (§ 6: hosting rates not to exceed those charged to any other party, plus one-year price freeze). Keep as drafted. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 5 COMPENSATION. | § 5(a) take-or-pay monthly minimums for Hosting and Support regardless of services requested; § 6 removes our documentation and dispute rights for those minimums. Dollar figures still blank. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review *(verification: fail)* | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicit, no-hire or inducement covenant binds us — our preferred position. Duration and carve-out checks are structurally inapplicable. Diligence the separate Non-Competition Agreement referenced in § 8(d). |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 13 gives acceptable one-year renewals on mutual 30-day notice, but there is no vendor renewal reminder and renewal pricing is uncapped (§ 6 freezes hosting costs for year one only). |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No obligation on TrueLink to provide transition assistance, return our data in usable format, or delete it; §§ 10, 13 and 14 are all silent. Material in a hosting deal holding borrower and loan data. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | § 9 warrants Y2K date handling only; no professional/workmanlike, conformance, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy, while § 12 disclaims all implied warranties. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance provision anywhere (§§ 13–30 contain none). TrueLink's indemnity and the liability cap are unsupported by any insurance backstop. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the positions we should treat as non-negotiable; the first is expressly identified in our playbook as a walk-away scenario.

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped Vendor (LOL-CAP, § 12).** An arrangement in which our liability — including our broad § 12(a) indemnity — is entirely uncapped while TrueLink is capped at 12 months' compensation paid is the playbook walk-away. We require: a **mutual** cap at the greater of 12 months' fees **paid or payable** and **USD 1,000,000**; a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages; and carve-outs from the cap for indemnities, confidentiality and data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, with confirmation that our payment obligations are not "damages".
2. **No Vendor IP infringement indemnity or duty to defend (INDEMN, § 12).** We cannot accept a hosted-services and interface licence with no third-party IP infringement indemnity and no duty to defend. We require the defence obligation plus IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs, with a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure.
3. **Mandatory sole-source credit report tie (EXCLUSIVITY, § 3(i)).** The obligation to order a TrueLink credit report on every borrower underwritten through the Interface, uncapped and with no exit for TrueLink's failure to meet the § 3 and § 4 response-time, availability and support commitments, is worse than our fallback and close to walk-away. Minimum acceptable outcome is a 12-month, category-limited commitment that terminates on TrueLink performance failure.

---

## 4. Next steps

**Tier 1 — must resolve before signature (critical/high):**

1. **§ 12 (Indemnity):** add TrueLink's defence obligation and the IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct indemnities, plus a standard indemnity procedure.
2. **§ 12 (Liability):** make the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; add the mutual indirect-damages exclusion; carve out indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement and our payment obligations.
3. **§ 15 (Assignment):** add our affiliate/successor (M&A) carve-out, a "not unreasonably withheld" consent standard, a bar on TrueLink assigning to a Client competitor, and confirmation that a Client change of control is neither an assignment nor a TrueLink termination trigger.
4. **§ 2 (New 2(e)):** confirm our ownership of Client Content, Client IP and data; assign Support Services work product to us with a licence back for embedded TrueLink IP; no joint ownership. Preserve the negotiated Credit Data licence in § 8(d).
5. **§ 2 / § 8(c) / § 13(b):** extend the licence to our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, conform the access restriction, limit licence termination to **uncured material** breach, and add the successor-transfer carve-out.
6. **§ 14 (Termination):** state an express 30-day Client convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no penalty; confirm TrueLink has no mid-term convenience exit (its end-of-term 30-day non-renewal right is acceptable); correct the § 13 cross-reference from § 12 to § 14, and the § 6 cross-references to "Section 4".

**Tier 2 — priority commercial and operational items (medium):**

7. **§ 3(i):** convert the mandatory credit report order into an optional right and confirm no exclusive or sole-source purchasing obligation binds us (fallback per Section 3 above).
8. **§ 5(a) / § 6:** delete the monthly minimum fee floor so we pay only for Hosting and Support Services actually requested, and remove the consequential carve-outs from our documentation and dispute rights. The dollar figures remain blank, so this is a low-friction edit now. Fallback: a 12-month, notice-reducible true-up if TrueLink requires a revenue floor.
9. **§ 13:** add a 60-day TrueLink renewal and fee-change reminder and cap renewal increases at the lesser of CPI and 3% (fallback 5%).
10. **§ 14:** insert transition assistance, data return in usable format and certified deletion (fallback: 90 days' assistance with export within 30 days). Confirm coverage under the § 24 survival provision (§§ 5–30).
11. **§ 9:** insert a TrueLink performance and conformance warranty with a repair/replace/refund remedy, relying on the "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT" carve-out in the § 12 disclaimer.

**Tier 3 — lower priority and monitoring:**

12. **New § 31 (Insurance):** require CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request; conform the § 24 survival list so the one-year post-term coverage obligation survives.
13. **Hold the favourable positions:** resist any vendor audit right (fallback if conceded: annual, 15 days' notice, at TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%); resist any non-solicit (fallback if conceded: mutual, personnel directly involved, 12 months from end of involvement, general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire; walk away from any no-hire, any term beyond 24 months, or coverage of all Vendor personnel); retain the Vendor-granted MFN in § 6; leave governing law and venue as drafted.
14. **Out-of-document diligence:** obtain and review the separate **Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in § 8(d). Within this agreement it operates only as a limitation on TrueLink's use of our Credit Data, but it should be reviewed on its own terms for any restraint or personnel restriction binding us."}
